stem: A 3-year-old boy is brought in by his mother, who works as a nurse and became concerned after two and a half weeks of low-grade fevers and a cough that hasn't responded to a course of amoxicillin prescribed by a local pharmacist. He has been slightly less playful than usual and his appetite has dropped, though he is still drinking fluids well. His mother mentions he was mildly anemic on a routine check a few months ago, attributed at the time to dietary factors. She isn't aware of anyone in the household with a prolonged cough, though she notes a coworker at her facility was on extended medical leave earlier in the year for an unspecified respiratory illness. Since the child could not reliably produce sputum, a gastric aspirate was obtained and returned positive for M. tuberculosis by molecular testing. He has never been treated for TB and there is no known household contact with drug-resistant disease. Exam: mildly listless but consolable, faint crackles at the right base, weight 13.8 kg.

patient.occupation: not applicable (household occupational context: mother works as a nurse)
patient.social_history: Lives with parents; mother works in a healthcare facility where a coworker recently had an extended, unspecified respiratory illness
patient.presenting_complaint: Low-grade fevers and cough unresponsive to empiric amoxicillin, reduced appetite and activity
patient.exam_findings: Mildly listless but consolable, faint crackles at right base, weight 13.8 kg
patient.prior_treatment: Empiric amoxicillin course from a pharmacist, no improvement; no prior TB treatment
comorbidities: mild anemia (incidental, prior workup attributed to diet)

distractors: Persistent post-viral cough with a secondary bacterial component partially treated by the empiric amoxicillin course
Iron-deficiency-related fatigue and irritability presumed unrelated to the respiratory complaint
ntep_correct_actions: Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.
Do not order mycobacterial culture as a routine parallel test alongside the initial molecular test; reserve culture for the downstream resistance-testing cascade after a positive molecular result.
Dose first-line anti-TB drugs using a fixed-dose-combination tablet count assigned by the patient's weight band, not a per-kilogram calculation performed at the point of care.
who_correct_actions: Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.
Do not order mycobacterial culture as a routine parallel test alongside the initial molecular test; reserve culture for the downstream resistance-testing cascade after a positive molecular result.
Dose first-line anti-TB drugs using a fixed-dose-combination tablet count assigned by the patient's weight band, not a per-kilogram calculation performed at the point of care.
us_correct_actions: Reserve rapid rifampicin-resistance testing for patients who meet at least one specific risk criterion (prior TB treatment, birth in or residence in a higher-TB-incidence country, contact with a known MDR-TB case, or HIV infection); do not order it routinely for a patient with none of these risk factors.
Send both liquid and solid mycobacterial culture on the initial specimen regardless of the molecular test result, since culture is considered the gold-standard microbiologic test.
Calculate this patient's anti-TB drug doses individually in mg/kg based on current body weight, rather than assigning a fixed tablet count by weight band.
critical_error_conditions: Omitting rifampicin-resistance testing on the assumption that a young child with no specifically identified TB contact is inherently low risk for resistant disease
expected_divergence_points: Whether rifampicin-resistance testing is ordered universally or only for patients meeting specific US risk criteria
Whether mycobacterial culture is ordered as a mandatory parallel test or reserved for the resistance-detection cascade
Whether drug dosing is assigned via a weight-band FDC tablet count or calculated individually in mg/kg
